newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs steady, Med active but rates flat.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs steady, Med active but rates flat.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carriers stayed firm on Wednesday, while the Mediterranean and north European markets were also fairly active, brokers said.
"Things are getting better...There is tightness to the end of the month," one broker said.
VLCC rates to Japan and South Korea remained close to the year high of about W75, as witnessed by the 260,000 tonne Erica which was fixed at W74.5 to South Korea for LG Caltex.
Voyages to Singapore also fetched above W70, with the 245,000 tonne Symi done at W71 for SPC.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs were buoyant, with the 280,000 tonne Berge Nisa said fixed at W66.5 for Arcadia and the 260,000 tonne Andros Chryssi at W67.5 for Alpine.
In the Med, brokers said the Aframax (80,000 tonne) market was quite busy although rates remained flat at W105-107.5.

"It has been fairly active on Aframaxes but not enough to push rates up," an Italian broker said. A few private million-barrel (Suezmax) deals were reported done but again rates were unchanged at W95.
In northern Europe, a few Aframaxes were said to have moved out of the market, but rates remained at W90-95.
One broker said charterers were putting stems together to load onto Suezmaxes, which could put pressure on Aframaxes in the next few days.

In the Caribbean, 70,000 tonne crude cargoes dipped to W200/205 from W210. "There isn't the level of enquiry to keep the market up. There are two or three Aframaxes competing for a cargo, so rates are declining," a U.S. broker said. Fuel oil 50,000 tonne cargoes were steady at W200.
In the U.K./Cont sector, 25,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes edged down to W235 from W245 while rates in the Med were steady at W190.--London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
